items.title: TN Police book DMK MP A Raja, Sekar Babu over remarks against CM Vijay
items.summary: The Tamil Nadu Police have registered cases against three senior Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) leaders over alleged derogatory remarks against Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay and Law Minister CT Nirmal Kumar. The cases were filed against DMK deputy general secretary and Nilgiris MP A Raja, Harbour MLA PK Sekar Babu and Rishivandiyam MLA Vasantham Karthikeyan following protests held by the party on September 12. The DMK had organised statewide demonstrations to protest Vijay’s remarks in the Assembly on September 7 concerning party president MK Stalin’s detention under the Maintenance of Internal Security Act (MISA) during the Emergency. In Chennai, Saidapet police registered a case against Raja based on a complaint from TVK functionary Karthik. The charges against him include intentionally insulting with intent to provoke breach of peace and statements conducing to public mischief and insulting the modesty of a woman. The complaint alleged that Raja made derogatory remarks against Nirmal Kumar during the protest. Raja had criticised the minister for questioning the circumstances surrounding Stalin’s detention. At the protest, Raja described Vijay as a “great scoundrel” while questioning the minister’s remarks on Stalin’s MISA detention. He also allegedly made comments questioning Nirmal Kumar’s parentage, which were seen as insulting his mother. The remarks drew criticism, including from within the DMK. DMK MP Kanimozhi Karunanidhi posted a Thirukkural couplet on controlling one’s tongue, which was widely interpreted as a response to Raja. CPI(M) state secretary P Shanmugam also criticised the remarks, saying it was “unbearable” that some DMK leaders continued to demean women while cadres cheered them. Raja later expressed regret over his comments in a post on X. “I regret that, in an emotional impulse, I questioned the identity of the person who repeatedly and deliberately mocked a leader who was born out of sacrifice, by calling his identity a lie. I have no hesitation in taking back my words. If you do not mend your ways, you will be made to do so,” he wrote. A separate case was registered at North Beach Police Station against Sekar Babu, based on a complaint alleging that he made derogatory remarks against Vijay and Nirmal Kumar during a protest near the Chennai Collectorate.
